questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Use only the front brake.
Avoid sudden movements.
Ride on the shoulder away from other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden movements.
questions.explanation: Ride safely on slippery surfaces by using both brakes when needed, slowing down, and avoiding sudden movements. Watch out for oily areas, shaded spots, dirt, gravel, and bridges—these have less grip than regular road surfaces.

questions.question: When adjusting your rearview mirror, make sure you can:

options.text: See the lane behind you and the lane next to you.
See only the lane behind you.
See only the lane next to you.
See most of your helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: See the lane behind you and the lane next to you.
questions.explanation: Set your mirror so you can see the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane next to you. A properly adjusted mirror may show the edge of your arm or shoulder, but the road behind and beside you is what matters most.

questions.question: Slippery surfaces make motorcycles hard to control. Which is a slippery surface?

options.text: Wet pavement
A driveway
Dry pavement
A parking lot

questions.correctAnswerText: Wet pavement
questions.explanation: Slippery surfaces include wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers in the road. Ride extra carefully on these surfaces.

questions.question: Alcohol does not need to be digested like food and drinks. This means:

options.text: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts to affect the drinker.
Alcohol never leaves the body.
It takes a long time to feel alcohol's effects.
Your body gets rid of alcohol very quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts to affect the drinker.
questions.explanation: Alcohol enters the bloodstream quickly without needing digestion and reaches the brain in minutes. Your body removes alcohol slowly—about one drink per hour.

questions.question: Motorcycle signals:

options.text: Are not important since motorcycles are small.
Are very important to tell other drivers what you plan to do.
Should not be used when no vehicles are nearby.
Are more complicated than car signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are very important to tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: As a motorcycle rider, you are vulnerable. Always use turn signals to tell others your plans. Signal every time you change lanes or turn, even if you think no one is nearby.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Hide your plans from other drivers.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Help you see others and be seen.
Keep you close to road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see others and be seen.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and lets them see you. It keeps you away from wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. It also discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: A motorcycle rider can improve visibility by:

options.text: Wearing dark-colored clothing.
Turning off the headlight.
Following other vehicles very closely.
Wearing bright-colored clothing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing bright-colored clothing.
questions.explanation: To be seen by other drivers, wear bright-colored clothing with reflective material, keep your headlight on at all times, and use your signals and brake light correctly.

questions.question: Which does not protect a motorcycle rider?

options.text: A leather jacket
Boots that cover the ankle
A tight baseball cap
Gloves

questions.correctAnswerText: A tight baseball cap
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles, and durable gloves to stay protected.

questions.question: If a friend has drunk too much and wants to ride their motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Let them ride.
Tell them to use quiet roads.
Stay out of it.
Take their keys.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take their keys.
questions.explanation: Never allow someone who has drunk too much to ride. Do whatever it takes to stop them, including taking their keys. Arrange another way for them to get home.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Have a seat that is large enough for two riders.
Only have one set of footrests.
Not encourage the passenger to wear protective clothing.
Put a sticker on the brake light to warn other motorists that a passenger is on the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a seat that is large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must have a seat large enough for two riders. It should also have footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear that you wear.

questions.question: Common drugs, such as cold tablets:

options.text: Can affect a rider's abilities to safely operate their motorcycle.
Usually won't affect a rider's abilities to safely operate their motorcycle.
Pose no risk to a rider's operating abilities.
Are always acceptable to take before riding because they are sold over-the-counter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect a rider's abilities to safely operate their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Almost all drugs, including over-the-counter medications, can affect your ability to ride safely. Know the side effects of any drug before you ride.

questions.question: Which of the following is not important when looking for a motorcycle helmet?

options.text: The helmet meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
The helmet fits snugly all the way around your head.
The helmet has no obvious defects, such as cracks or loose padding.
The helmet looks cool.

questions.correctAnswerText: The helmet looks cool.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. DOT standards, fits snugly around your head, and has no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. How it looks is not important for safety.

questions.question: To lessen your chances of being involved in an accident, you should:

options.text: Ride within a foot of the vehicle in front of you.
Wear dark clothing.
Signal only when you feel like it.
Stay alert and be prepared to act to avoid a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay alert and be prepared to act to avoid a crash.
questions.explanation: To reduce crashes, stay visible to others. Use your signals and brake light. Keep safe distance from other vehicles. Scan the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: Which of the following is not an example of a slippery surface?

options.text: A dirt or gravel road
A strip of oil in the center of a lane
Mud on pavement
Dry pavement

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Slippery surfaces include wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and oil. Dry pavement provides good traction.

questions.question: Keep an expanded cushion of space between your motorcycle and the vehicle in front of you:

options.text: When conditions will make stopping more difficult than usual.
When you want to look at the scenery.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.
To prevent the driver in front of you from knowing you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: When conditions will make stopping more difficult than usual.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space when stopping takes longer than normal. Increase your distance on slippery roads, when you cannot see ahead, or when traffic is heavy.

questions.question: To receive maximum protection, wear a helmet that is certified by the:

options.text: U.S. Department of Transportation.
Federal Trade Commission.
Federal Transportation Network.
National Association of Helmets.

questions.correctAnswerText: U.S. Department of Transportation.
questions.explanation: Wear a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards for maximum protection.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Not wear a jacket if it's warm out.
Always wear a jacket, even if it's warm out.
Wear shorts in warm weather.
Not be concerned about long shoelaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket, even if it's warm out.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket, even in warm weather. It protects you and helps prevent dehydration. Always wear long pants. Tuck in your shoelaces so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. Follow all rules posted on these signs.

questions.question: Which of the following should you inspect during a pre-ride check?

options.text: The general wear and tread of your tires
The amount of cushion your seat has
The shine of your paint
The wind direction

questions.correctAnswerText: The general wear and tread of your tires
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, tail light, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: Mirror checks should:

options.text: Be part of your normal checking routine.
Be avoided because they distract you.
Be avoided because other drivers can see you.
Only be done in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be part of your normal checking routine.
questions.explanation: You need to know what is behind you. Check your mirrors often as part of your regular driving routine.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, you should ride:

options.text: In any part of the lane.
In the part of the lane closest to the shoulder.
Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
As close to the car as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. This usually means riding in the center of the lane. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than their side mirrors, so this position helps them see you.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Ride faster than usual.
Use only the front brake.
Slow down.
Use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down on slippery surfaces. Use both brakes when braking and avoid sudden movements.

questions.question: If you ride on the right side of your lane while following a car:

options.text: You are in the best position to be seen.
The driver may not see you unless they use their side mirror.
The driver will assume you are there.
You are preventing other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may not see you unless they use their side mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than their side mirrors, so this position helps them see you.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should constantly look ahead for:

options.text: Road conditions.
Traffic conditions.
Escape routes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Look ahead to watch for changing traffic, hazardous road conditions, and ways to escape danger. Be ready to react to any changes.
